questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have also wanted to go but the nature and the people were a big part of the reason I choose Australia. Have always heard so much about the country and I thought this was the best way to experience it.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was preet easy. They gave you everything you needed to know in the introduction day and the persons to contact if you needed anything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any as I don't think you'll need that much assistance when you arrive as most things are pretty much all done. The only thing could be classes but they are helpfull with that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: pretty easy as there are a lot of offers for housing but it depends on what you are searching for. But if you just ask students who have been there before they can help you find the sites you'll need to find housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it's better than living on campus and I would strongly recommend doing this instead even if it seems easier to just let them do if for you so you don't have to stress about it. Try to find it yourself as it's cheaper and better.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy process as they guided you the whole way through with reminders of when you had to do certain things and what.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We had a student coordinator who you could always contact if there was anything you neeeded or just had a question. This was really helpfull and you shoulnd't worry about contacting to much as one too much is better than one to little.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty successful as I got the classes I registered for but not necessarily the was I wanted but just try to registre for as many as you can as you can then choose the ones that sounds most interesting.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the instructions and it will be a walk in the park and ask questions if you have any.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would say the level was average and you shouldn't worry about that at all. It's almost the same as UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Bit different as I'm used to more of a class were here it was big lectures. Here they are also more focused on you

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Quantitative Business Analysis, Quantitative Methods in Economics, International Trade, Learning in Outdoor Education

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Learning in Outdoor Education would be my biggest recommendation to any student. It's a course were you learn about the outdoors in Australia and where you get to go on hikes with your class and even a weekend trip.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I wouldn't say there were any unexpedted cost. It will depend on the travels you do as they sometimes came unexpeted and suddenly as you sometimes just decided to go as there was space in your calendar.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transport was more expensive then i thought but you can get a commision card for students but it's still a bit expensive. The. food and drinks are less expensive than i thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many but the problem is that many of the outdoor sports were done for the 2 semester as they had the finals in september so you couldn't sign up for any of those which is pretty frustrating but there are still many others to choose from.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do some sports as it's a good way to learn other people and as well learn about Australian culture through sports.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Not anything particulary but just to go on as many trips as you through out the semester even if it is just a day trip or a little week. Just go and enjoy the country as you don't have to worry about the classes as you can keep up still.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: No problem at all. But in Sydney it's really an international culture so everybody can fit in. But even outside of Sydney it's so easy as they are so easy to talk with and they just welcome you in like it's nothing at all.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just go out and be open for anything. Go to the events at school and try to talk to them in class as most are open to talk and hear about your culture as well.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: THe biggest difference is how international Sydney is compared to Copenhagen. There are so many nationalities but I wouldn't say there was anything that was challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness from everybody. It was so easy to fit in as everybody have done the same thing and if not they know how it can be.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Just be open for the adventures and experiences you get along the way. Don't miss out on anything because you stress about the courses you pnly have to pass so enjoy your time there and have fun.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do your research on the courses and what are available to you before you get there as it will be much easier and less stressfull.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people you meet and get to know. I thought it would have been the things you see which have also been so rewarding but the people you meet is the most rewarding thing I would say. So you be open to meet and talk to as many as you can.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having time to do all the things you wanted to and as well what you wanted to prioritise instead of others things.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
